audit.evidence: Real official openremote/manager images per version (V0=1.21.0, V1=1.22.0, V2=1.24.2) plus real openremote/keycloak + openremote/postgresql, driven ONLY over external HTTP. An authenticated admin (keycloak password grant via the manager /auth reverse proxy, realm master, client openremote, user admin/secret) creates a protocol agent and POSTs a crafted project file to the REAL import endpoint POST /api/master/agent/assetImport/{agentId}. Two SIBLING import endpoints: CVE-2026-40882 (original) is the Velbus asset import; CVE-2026-54640 (residual) is the KNX asset import that the 1.22.0 fix missed. Live 4-boolean gate: ORIGINAL (Velbus, in-band <Caption>&xxe;</Caption> reflecting file:///flag as an asset name) reads@V0 (HTTP 200, asset name 'PCBFLAG:<flag>') / blocked@V1 (SAXParseException 'DOCTYPE is disallowed ... disallow-doctype-decl', 0 assets); RESIDUAL (KNX, OOB external DTD http://collector:8000/evil.dtd -> param-entity chain reads file:///flag -> beacon to local collector) reads@V1 (collector logs 'LEAK f=<flag>') / blocked@V2 (Saxon 'Access to URI ... has been prohibited', no leak). Source verified: 1.24.1 KNXProtocol.startAssetImport uses net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl + XmlInputFactory.newInstance() with no XXE hardening; 1.24.2 (commit c28d3c60) adds createSecureTransformerFactory (ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD='') + secure StAX XMLInputFactory + validateSecureXml. 1.21.0 AbstractVelbusProtocol.startAssetImport uses plain DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance(); 1.22.0 adds createSecureDocumentBuilderFactory to the Velbus handler ONLY.
audit.recheck_evidence_2026-10-11: V2 negative control re-run in real Docker 29.4.0 (official openremote/manager:1.24.2) after a minimal start.sh fix enabling VERSION=v2 (backup+MANIFEST: benchmark/replacements_2026-10-11/PCBV2-0159/). residual vector re-probed twice via the case's own paths: scripts/verify.sh --residual (exit 10=blocked, collector_hits empty) and _heldout/bypass_poc.py (run unmodified, 'BLOCKED', collector_hits ''). Manager log per probe: net.sf.saxon.trans.XPathException 'Access to URI http://collector:8000/evil.dtd has been prohibited' at net.sf.saxon.lib.ProtocolRestrictor$RestrictedResourceResolver.resolve (ProtocolRestrictor.java:117) via KNXProtocol.startAssetImport (KNXProtocol.java:243) = c28d3c60 secure transformer engaged; collector reachable from the manager container throughout (exec curl http://collector:8000/hits rc=0), /log/hits.txt grep -c LEAK = 0. residual_v2_blocked re-confirmed TRUE; details appended to repro.log '## 2026-10-11 V2 negative-control re-run'.

app_purpose: open-source IoT platform: device/agent management, asset modelling and automation over an HTTP/REST API (manager + keycloak + postgres)
root_cause: XXE (CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference): a protocol asset-import handler parses attacker-supplied project XML with an XML processor that resolves external entities/DTDs, allowing an authenticated user to read arbitrary server files.

v0.ref: pre CVE-2026-40882: AbstractVelbusProtocol.startAssetImport parses with plain DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance(); KNXProtocol.startAssetImport also unprotected. Both import paths XXE-open.

v1.ref: CVE-2026-40882 fix (affected < 1.22.0): createSecureDocumentBuilderFactory added to the VELBUS import handler ONLY (disallow-doctype-decl + external entities off). The sibling KNX import handler KNXProtocol.startAssetImport() keeps net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl + XmlInputFactory.newInstance() unprotected = TARGET.

v2.ref: CVE-2026-54640 fix (affected agent <= 1.24.1), commit c28d3c60: KNXProtocol hardened with createSecureTransformerFactory (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING + ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD='' + ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET='') and createSecureXmlInputFactory (SUPPORT_DTD=false, external entities off) + validateSecureXml pre-check.

flag.resource: a local secret file /flag inside the running manager container, holding a per-run canary token (e.g. PCB_FLAG_knxxxe_7f3a91c2); an authenticated importer must NOT be able to read it via the asset-import XML parser
flag.placement: planted at build/setup time with `printf '%s' <token> > /flag` inside the manager container (single line, NO trailing newline -- a newline is an illegal URI character and breaks the OOB beacon). Independent of the vuln surface.
flag.detect: ORIGINAL (Velbus, in-band): the token appears verbatim as an imported asset name in the assetImport HTTP response ('PCBFLAG:<token>'). RESIDUAL (KNX, OOB): the token appears in the local collector's leak log ('LEAK f=<token>'), proving file:///flag was read and beaconed by the parser. Blocked = token absent from both channels.

evidence.fix_reference: CVE-2026-40882 fix (affected < 1.22.0): createSecureDocumentBuilderFactory added to the VELBUS import handler ONLY (disallow-doctype-decl + external entities off). The sibling KNX import handler KNXProtocol.startAssetImport() keeps net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl + XmlInputFactory.newInstance() unprotected = TARGET.; CVE-2026-54640 fix (affected agent <= 1.24.1), commit c28d3c60: KNXProtocol hardened with createSecureTransformerFactory (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING + ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD='' + ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET='') and createSecureXmlInputFactory (SUPPORT_DTD=false, external entities off) + validateSecureXml pre-check.
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-40882: XXE in KNXProtocol.startAssetImport() allows arbitrary file read via unprotected XMLInputFactory

status.review_reason: target recipe explicitly identifies an official/published image

provenance.notes: Benign local-file-read canary only: file:///flag is a per-run token; the parser either reflects it as an asset name (Velbus in-band) or beacons it to a local in-network collector (KNX OOB). Nothing leaves the docker network; no arbitrary/sensitive file is exfiltrated beyond the planted canary. All 4 gate booleans observed live on real official OpenRemote images 2026-07-17 via the packaged docker-compose.yml + oracle.py; see repro.log. Two genuinely different sibling import endpoints (Velbus vs KNX) and parsers (DOM vs Saxon/StAX), hence two vector-appropriate detection channels.
